sources.title: suomi.fi
highlights: However, e-services require a tool that enables you to use strong identification online

sources.title: ihhelsinki.fi
highlights: Banks in Finland require a foreigner’s identity card issued by the Finnish authorities to enable non-EU nationals use online banking credentials for strong identification
A visit to the selected bank is required
It is most convenient to get the Finnish ID card first and then go to the bank to open a bank account and strong identification at the same time
The processing time varies between banks and when first appointment times are available

sources.title: s-pankki.fi
highlights: Huomioithan, että tarvitset suomalaisen henkilötunnuksen ennen kuin voit saada sähköisen tunnistusvälineen, jota tarvitaan esimerkiksi viranomaispalveluihin tunnistautumiseen
Ilman suomalaista henkilötunnusta voit saada käyttöösi vain rajoitetut verkkopankkitunnukset, joita ei voi käyttää muihin palveluihin, kuten viranomaispalveluihin tunnistautumiseen

sources.title: poppankki.fi
highlights: To be granted a strong electronic means of identification, you must have a Finnish personal identity code and be entered in the Population Information System

sources.title: nordea.fi
highlights: You can obtain online banking credentials and a strong electronic ID when you become a customer, provided you have a valid identity document required for this purpose
A valid identity document and a residence permit for Finland

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: Describes a realistic timeline of roughly 5–10 days once documents are complete (verify on op.fi
Book the appointment in advance — walk-in service for new account openings is not guaranteed, and at busy branches the wait for a slot can itself add days

OP notes that the most common reason applications are delayed is incorrect or incomplete registration details, so it is worth double-checking that your name and address at DVV exactly match what you give the bank
Non-EU citizens may need extra steps (for example a Finnish ID card) to enable strong electronic identification

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: Ask the bank explicitly that your codes are enabled for strong electronic identification, not only for banking
Nordea describes a workaround used in Finland: you can visit a police station, where your identity is verified so the electronic identification service can be activated
